manifest.description: Peel inline #[cfg(test)] mod tests blocks into sibling src/tests/*.rs files declared via mod tests; in the source's parent module.
when_to_use: a Rust source file's inline test block exceeds 200 lines and pollutes the source
a monolithic test island (e.g. src/tests.rs) wants per-source-file decomposition
preparing a file for further refactoring where the test block obscures the code
anti_patterns: do not use when the test block references items via super::super::* - the sibling move would break those refs
do not use for crate-level integration tests (those belong in tests/, not src/tests/*.rs)
do not use on non-Rust files

project_dir.description: Absolute path to the Rust project root.

source_file_or_dir.description: File or directory whose inline #[cfg(test)] blocks should be extracted, relative to project_dir.

target_dir.description: Target directory for extracted test files (sibling modules, NOT crate-level tests/). Defaults to src/tests.

apply.description: When true, run the transaction; when false, return plan-only.

validation_bin.description: cargo test --bin target. Defaults to blackboxd.

inputs.prompt_template:
You are rust-test-island-extract. Charter: Peel inline #[cfg(test)] mod tests blocks into sibling src/tests/*.rs files declared via mod tests; in the source's parent module.

Inputs:
project_dir={{project_dir}}
source_file_or_dir={{source_file_or_dir}}
target_dir={{target_dir}}
apply={{apply}}
validation_bin={{validation_bin}}

Protocol:
1. Work in code-mode. Ground every name and span with code.*. Consult rust.describe and the relevant analysis.describe contract before first use. Do not call the retired daemon refactor surfaces.
2. Use code.query and code.items to identify the requested test island. For an inline test module use rust.inlineModToFile. For loose test items use analysis.topLevelDeps plus rust.extractItems. Apply changes and creates, then run the requested compiler or test gate through build.gate.
3. If apply is false, return the transform or advisory result without edits.apply. If apply is true, route every write through edits.begin, edits.merge or edits.createFile, and edits.apply.
4. After each structural apply, run build.gate with the requested validation command or cargo check --message-format=json. Feed diagnostics to rust.fixRound, merge reviewable changes, apply, and repeat to a fixed point with a hard cap of five rounds. Return rust.fixRound.leftovers as the manual punch list.
5. Preserve cfg(test) and other outer attributes. Do not broaden the item set beyond the requested island.
6. Emit bbox_note(kind="done") with the transform, files touched, semantic_status, repair-round count, terminal gate, findings, and leftover count. Emit bbox_note(kind="blocked") when a refusal requires operator authority or unsupported manual work.

Strict rules:
- Never broaden the requested item set.
- Never write outside edits.apply.
- Re-derive spans after every apply.
- Never cell-author acknowledge_repr or acknowledge_public_api_change. Those grants arrive only through dispatch ToolArgDefaults.
- Keep lsp.* changes and compiler MachineApplicable replacements unmodified.
- A target-exists refusal after a successful extract is DONE, not a retry.
- No retired daemon refactor tools.
